## O que acabou de acontecer
Um spike provou uma virada de linguagem no motor de motion: em vez de **DESENHAR** formas do zero em
CSS (que produzia glifo genérico, círculo vazio, ícone sorteado por hash), o motor passa a **MONTAR**
camadas prontas num espaço 3D — screenshot real, PNG com alpha recortado, SVG — com perspectiva de
câmera, parallax geométrico e profundidade de campo.

**Veredito do Sovereign, literal:** *"ficou incrível. Era exatamente isso que eu estava falando, com
isso já conseguimos montar vídeos e canais com outras estratégias de canal dark, sem depender do Veo
em si. Preciso urgentemente que você documente isso e distribua para que nossa equipe de criação
consiga fazer mais desses vídeos em escala e usando nosso motor e ecossistema, com os nós do spaces,
agente chat e toda a equipe. Esse é o nosso produto — um concorrente direto do Veo que ao mesmo
tempo trabalha junto; um motor mecânico junto com motor elétrico."*

**A tese comercial (registre-a, é a razão de ser do módulo):** Veo cobra por segundo, é
não-determinístico e não aceita direção fina. Este motor custa **US$ 0 / 0 mco**, é
**determinístico** (mesmo seed ⇒ mesmo pixel) e aceita direção quadro a quadro. Não competem —
compõem: Veo entrega o fotorreal; MONTAR entrega dado, UI, marca, comparativo e ritmo.

## 4 · Perspectiva do `build-scene.mjs` — TRAPÉZIO REAL

Razão borda-esquerda/borda-direita, marcadores 0×0 nos cantos sob `window.__seek(2.4)`:

```
ANTES   [data-card=L] 1,0000 · [data-card=R] 1,0000 · [data-far] 1,0000   → RETÂNGULO
DEPOIS  [data-card=L] 1,1022 · [data-card=R] 0,9372 · [data-far] 1,0302/0,9706 → trapézio
```

O `will-change` era só metade: o JS punha **`opacity` e `filter` de verdade** nos `.pl` (`pl.cardL.style.opacity`, `pl.far.style.filter='blur(...)'`), e propriedade de agrupamento rebaixa `transform-style` para `flat` mesmo sem will-change. Então o plano virou geometria pura (`will-change:transform`) e opacidade/desfoque desceram para as folhas (lâmina, chip), com o produto de alfas preservando a composição de grupo em `wires`/`badge`. Custo no formato que vai rodar: **558 → 545 ms/f (ruído)**. Verifiquei o pixel: a lâmina esquerda agora tem bordas convergentes e lê como painel inclinado.

Observações honestas: os 10,2% ficam abaixo dos ~21% da referência — é consequência do `rotateY`/Z declarados, não do bug. `getComputedStyle().transformStyle` reportava `preserve-3d` o tempo todo (valor especificado), por isso a falha atravessou o spike inteiro.

> 267	<script>
> 268	(function(){
> 269	  var W=${W},H=${H},D=${D},P=${PERSP};
> 270	  var CAM=${JSON.stringify(CAM)}, Z=${JSON.stringify(Z)};
> 271	  var MS=[${MS_DESENHAR},${MS_MONTAR}];
> 272	
> 273	  function ease(x){ return x<=0?0:x>=1?1:1-Math.pow(1-x,3); }
> 274	  function smooth(x){ return x<=0?0:x>=1?1:x*x*(3-2*x); }
> 275	  function spring(x){ return x<=0?0:x>=1?1:1-Math.exp(-6*x)*Math.cos(9*x); }
> 276	  function clamp(v,a,b){ return v<a?a:v>b?b:v; }
> 277	  function seg(t,a,b){ return clamp((t-a)/(b-a),0,1); }
> 278	  function win(t,a,b,c,d){ return ease(seg(t,a,b))*(1-smooth(seg(t,c,d))); }
> 279	
> 280	  function camZ(t){
> 281	    for(var i=0;i<CAM.length-1;i++){
> 282	      if(t<=CAM[i+1][0]){
> 283	        var u=smooth((t-CAM[i][0])/(CAM[i+1][0]-CAM[i][0]));
> 284	        return CAM[i][1]+(CAM[i+1][1]-CAM[i][1])*u;
> 285	      }
> 286	    }
> 287	    return CAM[CAM.length-1][1];
> 288	  }
> 289	
> 290	  var cam=document.getElementById('cam');
> 291	  var pl={}; for(var k in Z) pl[k]=document.getElementById(k);
> 292	  var slabL=document.querySelector('[data-card="L"]'), slabR=document.querySelector('[data-card="R"]');
> 293	  var farEls=[].slice.call(document.querySelectorAll('[data-far]'));
> 294	  var chipEls=[].slice.call(document.querySelectorAll('[data-chip]'));
> 295	  var barEls=[].slice.call(document.querySelectorAll('[data-bar]'));
> 296	  var badge=document.querySelector('[data-badge]');
> 297	  var wires=document.getElementById('wires');
> 298	  var wp=[wires.querySelector('.wh'),wires.querySelector('.wc'),wires.querySelector('.wh2'),wires.querySelector('.wc2')];
> 299	  var titleEl=document.getElementById('title'),capEl=document.getElementById('cap');
> 300	  var kickEl=document.getElementById('kick'),ruleEl=document.getElementById('rule');
> 301	  var endEl=document.getElementById('end'),scrimEl=document.getElementById('scrim');
> 302	  var weaveEl=document.getElementById('weave');
> 303	
> 304	  var maxMs=Math.max(MS[0],MS[1],1), BAR_MAX=230;
> 305	
> 306	  function seek(t){
> 307	    if(t<0)t=0; if(t>D)t=D;
> 308	    var cz=camZ(t);
> 309	
> 310	    // ── A CÂMERA. Uma translação em Z + deriva suave. Tudo o mais é consequência da perspectiva.
> 311	    cam.style.transform='translate3d('+(Math.sin(t*0.40)*24).toFixed(2)+'px,'
> 312	      +(Math.cos(t*0.31)*13).toFixed(2)+'px,'+cz.toFixed(1)+'px)';
> 313	    // a textura do vazio obedece à MESMA câmera: escala = P/(P-eff), igual à projeção do plano.
> 314	    var wEff = cz + Z.grid, wS = P/(P-wEff);
> 315	    weaveEl.style.transform='translate('+(Math.sin(t*0.40)*24*wS).toFixed(2)+'px,'
> 316	      +(Math.cos(t*0.31)*13*wS).toFixed(2)+'px) scale('+wS.toFixed(4)+')';
> 317	
> 318	    // ── FOCO: 5 estações. Lâmina esq → notificações (no vão) → lâmina dir → dado → recorte.
> 319	    //    A estação nas notificações é o que prova o DoF: o que está NO MEIO do corredor fica
> 320	    //    nítido enquanto as DUAS paredes ficam suaves. Isso só existe porque há Z de verdade.
> 321	    var focus = Z.cardL;
> 322	    focus += (Z.chips-focus)*smooth(seg(t,2.9,3.7));
> 323	    focus += (Z.cardR-focus)*smooth(seg(t,4.3,5.0));
> 324	    focus += (Z.data-focus)*smooth(seg(t,5.4,6.3));
> 325	    focus += (Z.cut-focus)*smooth(seg(t,7.6,8.8));
> 326	    function dof(z){ return clamp(Math.abs(z-focus)/80, 0, 11); }
> 327	
> 328	    for(var kk in Z) pl[kk].style.transform='translate3d(-50%,-50%,'+Z[kk]+'px)';
> 329	
> 330	    // ── TRAVESSIA (Família A) ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
> 331	    // Opacidade de GRUPO desce para as folhas: posta no plano, ela achata a perspectiva (ver .pl).
> 332	    // Para conteúdo que não se sobrepõe, alpha-por-folha == alpha-de-grupo; onde há sobreposição
> 333	    // (fios sob a lâmina), o produto abaixo reproduz a mesma composição.
> 334	    var opL=win(t,0.15,1.15,4.55,5.35);
> 335	    var opR=win(t,0.45,1.55,5.05,5.95);
> 336	    slabL.style.opacity=String(opL);
> 337	    slabR.style.opacity=String(opR);
> 338	    // a lâmina "abre" conforme a câmera passa — porta girando, não ruído
> 339	    var openL=28+10*smooth(seg(t,3.0,5.2))+Math.sin(t*0.5)*1.6;
> 340	    var openR=-26-9*smooth(seg(t,3.4,5.6))+Math.cos(t*0.45)*1.5;
> 341	    slabL.style.transform='rotateY('+openL.toFixed(2)+'deg) translateZ('+((1-ease(seg(t,0.15,1.25)))*-300).toFixed(1)+'px)';
> 342	    slabR.style.transform='rotateY('+openR.toFixed(2)+'deg) translateZ('+((1-ease(seg(t,0.45,1.65)))*-300).toFixed(1)+'px)';
> 343	    slabL.style.filter='blur('+dof(Z.cardL).toFixed(2)+'px)';
> 344	    slabR.style.filter='blur('+dof(Z.cardR).toFixed(2)+'px)';
> 345	
> 346	    badge.style.opacity=String(win(t,1.3,2.0,5.05,5.7)*opR);
> 347	    badge.style.transform='scale('+spring(seg(t,1.3,2.2)).toFixed(3)+')';
> 348	
> 349	    var d1='M 750 -160 C '+(750+Math.sin(t*0.8)*30)+' 220, 340 340, 250 540';
> 350	    var d2='M 750 -160 C '+(750+Math.cos(t*0.7)*26)+' 240, 1160 380, 1250 580';
> 351	    wp[0].setAttribute('d',d1); wp[1].setAttribute('d',d1);
> 352	    wp[2].setAttribute('d',d2); wp[3].setAttribute('d',d2);
> 353	    wires.style.opacity=String(win(t,0.8,1.9,4.9,5.8)*0.95*opR);
> 354	
> 355	    var farOp=win(t,0.0,1.3,3.9,4.8);
> 356	    var farBlur='blur('+dof(Z.far).toFixed(2)+'px)';
> 357	    for(var fq=0;fq<farEls.length;fq++){
> 358	      farEls[fq].style.opacity=String(farOp*0.5);
> 359	      farEls[fq].style.filter=farBlur;
> 360	    }
> 361	
> 362	    // ── notificações no corredor: entram DEPOIS do título sair, somem antes da travessia acabar
> 363	    var chipOp=win(t,2.8,3.6,4.9,5.6), chipBlur='blur('+dof(Z.chips).toFixed(2)+'px)';
> 364	    for(var q=0;q<chipEls.length;q++){
> 365	      chipEls[q].style.opacity=String(chipOp);
> 366	      chipEls[q].style.filter=chipBlur;
> 367	      var cin=Math.min(spring(seg(t,2.8+q*0.28,4.0+q*0.28)),1.05);
> 368	      chipEls[q].style.transform='rotateZ('+(q===0?-5:3.6)+'deg) rotateY('+(q===0?12:-12)+'deg) '
> 369	        +'translateY('+((1-cin)*34).toFixed(1)+'px)';
> 370	    }
> 371	
> 372	    // ── O DADO (Família B) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
> 373	    pl.data.style.opacity=String(ease(seg(t,5.2,6.3)));
> 374	    pl.data.style.filter='blur('+dof(Z.data).toFixed(2)+'px)';
> 375	    for(var b=0;b<barEls.length;b++){
> 376	      var grow=Math.min(spring(seg(t,5.5+b*0.20,7.0+b*0.20)),1.06);
> 377	      barEls[b].style.height=(BAR_MAX*(MS[b]/maxMs)*Math.max(grow,0)).toFixed(1)+'px';
> 378	      barEls[b].style.opacity=String(ease(seg(t,5.4+b*0.20,6.1+b*0.20)));
> 379	    }
> 380	
> 381	    // ── O RECORTE (Família C): entra por último, pela direita, e empurra na câmera ───────────
> 382	    var fIn=Math.min(spring(seg(t,7.4,8.9)),1.04);
> 383	    pl.cut.style.opacity=String(ease(seg(t,7.4,8.1)));
> 384	    pl.cut.style.transform='translate3d(calc(-50% + '+(104+(1-fIn)*430).toFixed(1)+'px),calc(-50% + 44px),'+Z.cut+'px) '
> 385	      +'rotateY('+(-15+Math.sin(t*0.45)*2.2).toFixed(2)+'deg)';
> 386	    pl.cut.style.filter='blur('+dof(Z.cut).toFixed(2)+'px)';
> 387	
> 388	    // ── HUD ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
> 389	    var hudOut=1-smooth(seg(t,3.0,3.8));
> 390	    kickEl.style.opacity=String(ease(seg(t,0.1,0.8))*hudOut);
> 391	    ruleEl.style.width=(210*ease(seg(t,0.25,1.3))).toFixed(1)+'px';
> 392	    ruleEl.style.opacity=String(hudOut);
> 393	    titleEl.style.opacity=String(ease(seg(t,0.45,1.5))*hudOut);
> 394	    titleEl.style.transform='translateY('+((1-ease(seg(t,0.45,1.6)))*24).toFixed(1)+'px)';
> 395	    capEl.style.opacity=String(ease(seg(t,1.7,2.6))*hudOut);
> 396	    var eOn=ease(seg(t,8.0,8.9));
> 397	    endEl.style.opacity=String(eOn);
> 398	    endEl.style.transform='translateY('+((1-eOn)*18).toFixed(1)+'px)';

> 400	    scrimEl.style.opacity=String(Math.max(ease(seg(t,0.1,0.9))*hudOut*0.95, eOn*0.90));
> 401	  }
> 402	
> 403	  window.__seek=seek;
> 404	  seek(0);
> 405	  window.__ready=true;
> 406	})();
> 407	</script></body></html>`;

> 314	async function processMotion(renderId: string, userId: string, comp: MotionComposition) {

> 340	    const asked = (Array.isArray(comp.elements) ? comp.elements.map(String) : []);

> 106	/** Até `max` ícones cujo keyword aparece no texto da cena, na ordem de aparição. */
> 107	export function detectContextIcons(text: string, max = 3): Array<{ id: string; path: string }> {
> 108	  const lower = text.toLowerCase();
> 109	  const hits: Array<{ id: string; path: string; pos: number }> = [];
> 110	  for (const [id, icon] of Object.entries(ICON_LIBRARY)) {
> 111	    let best = -1;
> 112	    for (const kw of icon.keywords) {
> 113	      const p = lower.indexOf(kw);
> 114	      if (p >= 0 && (best < 0 || p < best)) best = p;
> 115	    }
> 116	    if (best >= 0) hits.push({ id, path: icon.path, pos: best });
> 117	  }
> 118	  hits.sort((a, b) => a.pos - b.pos);
> 119	  return hits.slice(0, max).map(({ id, path }) => ({ id, path }));
> 120	}

> 122	/**
> 123	 * Extrai os SELOS (badges) que a direção pede, beat a beat.
> 124	 *
> 125	 * Por que isto existe: a linguagem v6 selada no EP05 usa o selo com entrada em spring como o
> 126	 * carimbo do dado-chave da cena (`CONSISTÊNCIA`, `GERE POUCO · REUSE MUITO`). Ao parametrizar o
> 127	 * motor, a CLASSE CSS `.badge` foi portada mas NADA nunca a instanciou — seis cenas do EP06 pedem
> 128	 * `badges` e nenhuma renderizava coisa alguma (perícia de 2026-08-05). Isto liga o elemento.
> 129	 *
> 130	 * O contrato de escrita já é o que a direção usa naturalmente: o texto do selo vem ENTRE ASPAS
> 131	 * dentro do beat — `badge '1M DE CONTEXTO' acende ao lado com spring`. Sem aspas não há selo:
> 132	 * inventar o texto seria pôr na tela uma palavra que ninguém escreveu (Lei 1).
> 133	 *
> 134	 * Tom: a direção diz `âmbar` quando o selo é uma ressalva ("MEDE O SISTEMA INTEIRO") — e ressalva
> 135	 * com a mesma cor do dado celebrado seria desonestidade visual.
> 136	 */
> 137	export function extractBadges(
> 138	  beats: Array<{ word: string; event: string }>,
> 139	): Array<{ text: string; beatIndex: number; tone: "ciano" | "ambar" }> {
> 140	  const out: Array<{ text: string; beatIndex: number; tone: "ciano" | "ambar" }> = [];
> 141	  beats.forEach((b, i) => {
> 142	    const ev = b.event ?? "";
> 143	    if (!/badge|selo|carimb/i.test(ev)) return;
> 144	    const quoted = ev.match(/['"«]([^'"»]{2,40})['"»]/);
> 145	    if (!quoted) return;
> 146	    const tone = /âmbar|ambar|ressalva|alerta|cuidado/i.test(ev) ? "ambar" : "ciano";
> 147	    out.push({ text: quoted[1].trim(), beatIndex: i, tone });
> 148	  });
> 149	  return out;
> 150	}

> 152	/**
> 153	 * O que a legenda mostra — e, quase sempre, o silêncio dela.
> 154	 *
> 155	 * Cena narrada não legenda: o narrador já carrega o sentido, e repetir texto na tela rouba a
> 156	 * atenção da imagem (a lição do teatro: o ator não mima o que diz). Sem narração, a cena precisa
> 157	 * de UMA frase — a primeira, INTEIRA, nunca cortada no meio da palavra como o motor fazia.
> 158	 */
> 159	export function screenCaption(description: string, narrated: boolean): string {
> 160	  if (narrated) return "";
> 161	  const first = String(description).split(/(?<=[.!?])\s+/)[0]?.trim() ?? "";
> 162	  if (first.length <= 110) return first;
> 163	  // corta na última palavra inteira dentro do limite e sinaliza a elisão
> 164	  const cut = first.slice(0, 110);
> 165	  return cut.slice(0, cut.lastIndexOf(" ")).trim() + "…";
> 166	}

> 173	function esc(s: string): string {
> 174	  return String(s)
> 175	    .replace(/&/g, "&amp;").replace(/</g, "&lt;").replace(/>/g, "&gt;")
> 176	    .replace(/"/g, "&quot;").replace(/'/g, "&#39;");

> 179	/**
> 180	 * Acha o número que MERECE virar contador na cena (2.800.000.000.000 · 1,8 milhão · 141.006 · 60x).
> 181	 *
> 182	 * Duas regras nasceram do Vision QA de 2026-08-04, e as duas são sobre honestidade numérica:
> 183	 *  1. `trilhoes` sem acento não casava com `trilh(ão|ões)` → 2,8 trilhões virava 2,8 e perdia para o
> 184	 *     "3" de "Kimi K3". Prefixo tolerante resolve.
> 185	 *  2. Número COM unidade sempre vence número solto — e número solto só entra se for grande (≥100),
> 186	 *     senão versões em nomes próprios ("K3", "v2", "GPT-5") viram contador e mentem na tela.
> 187	 *
> 188	 * A terceira nasceu do crítico adversarial da trupe (2026-08-05): a guarda `<100` engolia TODO
> 189	 * percentual — `76,8%` e `99,8%` devolviam `null`. Num canal sobre benchmarks isso apagava o dado
> 190	 * mais comum que existe. Unidade explícita (`%`/`x`) agora qualifica o número em qualquer magnitude.
> 191	 */
> 192	export function extractBigNumber(
> 193	  text: string,
> 194	): { value: number; label: string; unit: string; decimals: number } | null {
> 195	  const re = /(\d[\d.,]*)\s*(trilh\w*|bilh\w*|milh\w*|mil\b|%|x\b)?/gi;
> 196	  let best: { value: number; label: string; scaled: boolean; marked: boolean; unit: string; decimals: number } | null = null;
> 197	  for (const m of text.matchAll(re)) {
> 198	    const digits = m[1];
> 199	    const unit = (m[2] ?? "").toLowerCase();
> 200	    // pt-BR: ponto é separador de milhar, vírgula é decimal.
> 201	    const numeric = Number(digits.replace(/\./g, "").replace(",", "."));
> 202	    if (!Number.isFinite(numeric) || numeric === 0) continue;
> 203	
> 204	    let scale = 1;
> 205	    if (unit.startsWith("trilh")) scale = 1e12;
> 206	    else if (unit.startsWith("bilh")) scale = 1e9;
> 207	    else if (unit.startsWith("milh")) scale = 1e6;
> 208	    else if (unit.startsWith("mil")) scale = 1e3;
> 209	
> 210	    const scaled = scale > 1;
> 211	    const value = numeric * scale;
> 212	    // Unidade EXPLÍCITA (% ou x) torna o número um dado, qualquer que seja a magnitude.
> 213	    // A guarda `<100` existe só para rejeitar número de VERSÃO solto ("Kimi K3", "GPT-5.6") — e
> 214	    // versão nunca vem com "%". Sem esta distinção, TODO percentual abaixo de 100 era descartado
> 215	    // em silêncio: num canal sobre benchmarks, o dado mais comum que existe nunca virava contador
> 216	    // (achado do crítico adversarial da trupe, 2026-08-05: `extractBigNumber("76,8%")` → null).
> 217	    const marked = unit === "%" || unit === "x";
> 218	    if (!scaled && !marked && value < 100) continue;
> 219	    // escala (mil/milhão/…) vence unidade marcada, que vence número solto; empatados, o maior
> 220	    const rank = scaled ? 2 : marked ? 1 : 0;
> 221	    const bestRank = best ? (best.scaled ? 2 : best.marked ? 1 : 0) : -1;
> 222	    if (!best || rank > bestRank || (rank === bestRank && value > best.value)) {
> 223	      best = { value, label: m[0].trim(), scaled, marked, unit: marked ? unit : "", decimals: /[.,]\d/.test(digits) ? 1 : 0 };
> 224	    }
> 225	  }
> 226	  return best ? { value: best.value, label: best.label, unit: best.unit, decimals: best.decimals } : null;
> 227	}

## 🤖 Claude *(23:21:00)*

<details>
<summary>💭 Thinking Process</summary>

I'm mapping out how to integrate MONTAR as a full Spaces node capability, starting with a seam raster verb in the engine that layers PNGs and SVGs with alpha onto Z planes using perspective, pulling the camera and rendering approach from the existing build system.

The worker needs to resolve asset IDs server-side and download them into the working directory, failing loudly if anything's missing. The inspector should offer a real picker showing the project's available images with previews. Cost-wise, this stays free since rendering happens on the host—the node itself has zero debit, and any image generation costs are already accounted for by the nodes that created those assets.

For the data structure, I'm leaning toward adding a `layers` field to `MotionSceneData` where each layer specifies an asset ID, depth position (background, middle, foreground), horizontal alignment, scale, and optional tone adjustments, using a closed vocabulary to keep the spec predictable.

The trickier part is how `assets` fits into the elements list. I think the cleanest approach is to make `layers` the actual driver—if layers are declared, the server validates that `assets` is also in the elements list to keep things consistent and avoid silent drops. That way the UI toggle and the data structure stay honest with each other. — the UI Section displays the picker independently, not as a toggleable chip. So I'm leaning toward skipping the element token entirely and letting the `layers` array itself drive whether raster seams appear in the template. If `layers.length > 0`, the feature activates; otherwise it stays dormant. This sidesteps the legacy trap completely and keeps the data model clean.

The user won't be confused between the old dead "Imagens do projeto" chip and the new "Camadas de imagem" section since the chip is already gone from the selector. I can also improve the stale graph warning to point them toward the new section. The flow becomes: `layers: MotionLayer[]` on the scene data gets validated and resolved server-side (each asset scoped to its bucket and key), then composed into the template with relative paths like `layers/L0.png`, and the worker downloads each one into the workDir before Playwright loads them via `file://` protocol with `waitUntil: "load"`.

But `load` fires even if images fail to download, so I need two verification steps: the worker should validate each downloaded asset has real bytes and is actually an image (checking magic bytes or using ffprobe), and the template needs to wait for all layer images to decode successfully before setting `window.__ready`, which render-frames then checks before considering the render complete.

For error handling, instead of just timing out on a missing `__ready` signal, I'll have the template set `window.__fatal` with an error message if anything goes wrong, and render-frames can poll for either `__ready` or `__fatal` to exit cleanly with a clear error.

On the geometry side, the current template uses 2D positioning with per-element perspective transforms, but for proper 3D layering I need to restructure it with a dedicated 3D container that has `perspective` and `preserve-3d` enabled, placing the 3D elements behind the cards and HUD but above the background.

For the paint order, I'm thinking: background (galaxy) → 3D raster layers → edges SVG → cards and UI elements → icons → counters/charts/titles → final effects like vignette and bloom. The raster layers should sit behind the cards as the "set," though some elements like a hero cutout might need to be in front, so I'll use a depth vocabulary to organize the layers cleanly.

I'm settling on a single `#set` container with perspective that holds all planes, sorting them by Z-depth in descending order (far to near) to derive the paint order naturally. This keeps the stacking order honest to the spatial hierarchy. Both containers share the same perspective settings and camera transform to keep the geometry aligned. The camera only affects the raster planes, so existing 2D scenes stay unaffected—zero regression. When there are no layers, the containers are empty or omitted entirely, adding no overhead. For the camera motion, I'm using a monotonic dolly that scales proportionally to the scene duration, mirroring the spike's approach but adapted to whatever timeline we're working with.

I'm setting up a closed vocabulary for camera direction—`aproxima` for dolly in (the default), `afasta` for dolly out, and `fixa` for no dolly, just drift. This gives the camera control a real directorial feel with a fixed set of options. Each layer will have its own focus station for depth of field. The focus transitions happen automatically at each layer's entry beat, which keeps things clean. Each layer gets its own set of properties: an asset ID, a plane depth (background, middle, or foreground with specific Z values), horizontal alignment, scale factor, and a treatment type that determines whether it's a cutout with shadow or a solid block.

For the `laje` treatment, I'm adding a rotateY tilt that depends on alignment — left-aligned slabs rotate one direction, right-aligned rotate the opposite way, creating that door-opening effect from the spike. Cutouts get a subtle oscillating tilt instead. The key is keeping `will-change:transform` only on the plane container itself while opacity and filter effects stay on the inner layer element.

Now I'm working through the sizing: images have variable aspect ratios, so I'll use `width = baseW * scale` with `height:auto` for cutouts, but the slab gets a fixed box with `object-fit:cover`. Based on the spike's proportions, I'm setting the slab base to about 34% of stage width and cutouts to 24%, then scaling from there. I haven't tested 9:16 aspect ratios yet, but I can at least generate the HTML and validate the geometry through DOM measurement without heavy rendering cost — I'll note that as untested for now.

For the worker layer pipeline, I'm downloading each layer from Supabase storage, writing it locally with a numbered filename, verifying the magic bytes to confirm it's a valid image format, and checking that the file isn't empty — otherwise throwing a clear error. The scene spec then references these layers by their relative paths so the HTML template can find them.

The edge function accepts up to 6 layers with asset IDs and validates each one: resolving the asset from the user's scoped creative_assets table, ensuring the storage key is under the user's directory with no path traversal attempts, and confirming the asset kind is 'image'. If any validation fails, it returns a 422 with a specific message about which layer caused the problem.

Now I need to verify what kind values are actually allowed in the schema, check if there are test images available for user 0, and review the motion scene setup to add the layers field to the default state.

I also need to look at the SOP requirement — Amendment 43 gates the work until `docs/processes/motion-montar-camadas.md` exists. Since Lei 2 requires this documentation before code can proceed, I'll write the SOP as part of the deliverable to satisfy that constraint.

</details>

> #!/usr/bin/env python3
> """Self-host alpha matting with bare onnxruntime (no rembg install).
> Usage: matte.py <model.onnx> <in.png> <out.png> [--stroke N]
> """
> import sys, time
> import numpy as np
> import onnxruntime as ort
> from PIL import Image
> 
> model, src, dst = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3]
> stroke = 0
> if "--stroke" in sys.argv:
>     stroke = int(sys.argv[sys.argv.index("--stroke") + 1])
> 
> is_isnet = "isnet" in model
> 
> t0 = time.time()
> sess = ort.InferenceSession(model, providers=["CPUExecutionProvider"])
> t_load = time.time() - t0
> 
> inp = sess.get_inputs()[0]
> _, _, H, W = inp.shape
> H = 1024 if (not isinstance(H, int)) and is_isnet else (H if isinstance(H, int) else 320)
> W = H
> 
> img = Image.open(src).convert("RGB")
> ow, oh = img.size
> x = np.array(img.resize((W, H), Image.BILINEAR), dtype=np.float32)
> 
> if is_isnet:
>     x = x / 255.0
>     x = (x - 0.5) / 1.0
> else:
>     x = x / np.max(x)
>     x[:, :, 0] = (x[:, :, 0] - 0.485) / 0.229
>     x[:, :, 1] = (x[:, :, 1] - 0.456) / 0.224
>     x[:, :, 2] = (x[:, :, 2] - 0.406) / 0.225
> 
> x = np.transpose(x, (2, 0, 1))[None, ...].astype(np.float32)
> 
> t1 = time.time()
> out = sess.run(None, {inp.name: x})[0]
> t_infer = time.time() - t1
> 
> m = out[0, 0]
> m = (m - m.min()) / (m.max() - m.min() + 1e-8)
> mask = Image.fromarray((m * 255).astype(np.uint8), mode="L").resize((ow, oh), Image.BILINEAR)
> 
> rgba = img.convert("RGBA")
> rgba.putalpha(mask)
> 
> if stroke:
>     # sticker outline, like the "papel recortado" reference: dilate the matte and
>     # paint it white BEHIND the subject — hides matting fuzz by design.
>     import cv2
>     a = np.array(mask)
>     hard = (a > 128).astype(np.uint8) * 255
>     k = np.ones((stroke * 2 + 1, stroke * 2 + 1), np.uint8)
>     dil = cv2.dilate(hard, k, iterations=1)
>     base = Image.new("RGBA", (ow, oh), (255, 255, 255, 0))
>     base.putalpha(Image.fromarray(dil, mode="L"))
>     base.paste(rgba, (0, 0), rgba)
>     rgba = base
> 
> rgba.save(dst)
> a = np.array(rgba)[:, :, 3]
> semi = int(((a > 8) & (a < 247)).sum())
> print(f"model={model.split('/')[-1]} in={W}x{H} load={t_load:.2f}s infer={t_infer:.2f}s "
>       f"opaque={int((a>247).sum())} semi={semi} transparent={int((a<=8).sum())} -> {dst}")

I'm setting up the vocabulary for the motion layers system with TypeScript types for plane positioning, alignment, and treatment options, then starting to define the interface structure.

Now I'm completing the MotionLayer interface with asset reference and scale multiplier, adding a camera type for zoom control, and mapping out the Z-depth geometry table where each plane sits at a specific depth value. The camera movement modes will translate the camera position along the Z-axis to create approach and retreat effects.

I'm working through the math for perspective projection to ensure planes stay in front of the camera without distortion—calculating how the effective Z position (camera Z plus plane depth) affects the scale factor, and determining safe bounds to keep the effect visible and proportional. So the laje box should be portrait-oriented at 0.36W × 1.25H scaled, which gives a rendered height that overshoots the stage intentionally—that wall effect. But cropping a 16:9 image into that tall portrait box is harsh, so maybe I should let the image's natural aspect ratio guide the treatment instead.

I can detect the image's aspect ratio in the browser once it loads using `naturalWidth`, then size the laje box to match: width stays at W*0.40*scale, but height becomes width divided by the image's aspect ratio, capped at H*1.35 to prevent it from getting too tall. The recorte stays simpler—just the image with a drop-shadow at W*0.28*scale with auto height. Since the layout needs to happen after the image loads and `__ready` waits for that, I can apply the sizing at that point so the dimensions are correct.

The tricky part is that `seek(0)` currently runs synchronously right before setting `__ready=true`, but now I need to wait for images to load first. I'm restructuring the template to load all images, apply their sizes, then call `seek(0)` and set `__ready=true` once everything's ready—handling both success and failure cases for each image.

Writing image load handler... Within a preserve-3d container, the browser automatically depth-sorts by transformed position, so paint order follows Z naturally, though I'll keep them sorted explicitly in the DOM for stability. For placement, I'm putting the 3D world right after the background and before the edges, with raster layers behind the cards—but front-facing layers would also sit behind the cards, which could look wrong since the cards are semi-transparent glass with text overlays.

Given the design principle that the HUD sits outside the 3D space on a scrim, and the cards function more like content in the world itself, I'm splitting into two containers: one for background and middle layers before the edges, and another for front layers after the cards but before the text HUD. This way the cut-out sits closest to the viewer, with the title and legend as the true HUD layer above it. Both containers share the same perspective and camera transform—two identical camera elements is fine.

For depth of field, I'm calculating blur based on distance from the focus point, clamping the result to a reasonable range and applying it directly to the layer element itself, never the plane.

On entry, each layer animates in at its designated beat time with opacity easing and a translateZ offset that makes it appear from farther back. The leaf element handles the rotation and translation while the plane stays static—this mirrors how the spike handles its slabs. Now I'm working through the tilt alignment logic...

For the tilt angles, the left slab gets a positive rotation around 24 degrees, the right gets negative 24 degrees, and the center oscillates slightly or shifts based on the recorte setting. There's also a slow opening animation over time that increases the rotation gradually. For horizontal placement, the left layer sits at about 26% of the width to the left of center, the right mirrors that to the right, and center stays at zero—all positioned absolutely within the plane's coordinate system. Each layer gets its own plane element with a unique Z value plus a small per-index offset to prevent z-fighting and add subtle depth. The camera drift applies the same transform logic as before with small sine/cosine amplitude. The vignette effect is already in place. Now I'm thinking through the performance cost — each raster layer is an image with potential blur filtering, and the expense scales with the composited surface area, so a layer at roughly 0.4 of the viewport width composited at full scale on a 1920px canvas could be around 700×900 pixels.

At 1.5× device pixel ratio that's about 1.4 megapixels per layer, and with three layers plus blur effects I'm looking at roughly 4 megapixels total, which could add 200–400 milliseconds per frame. I need to measure this directly with the benchmark to see if it's actually a bottleneck. If it is, I can mitigate by only applying blur when the layer is larger than 0.3 pixels and capping the layer count at 4. Adding `will-change: transform` on the planes should help too.

I'm setting up the worker to download and verify each layer image from the bucket, checking that the bytes actually arrived and meet a minimum size threshold.

## 🤖 Claude *(23:24:23)*

<details>
<summary>💭 Thinking Process</summary>

I'm updating the preview runner to handle layer downloads using the service key to resolve asset IDs scoped to the project's user. Now I'm modifying the scene template to add raster layers and camera control options to the SceneSpec.

Defining the layer interface with plane depth positioning, alignment, treatment type, and scale properties. I'm also setting up depth constants for the three planes and camera travel distance, then exporting helper functions like `layerGeometry` and `cameraZ` so I can unit-test the camera invariant — ensuring the effective focal distance never crosses the camera plane across all time values and layer depths.

Writing the HTML injection code... Adding styling for the leaf and cutout layers...

The main concern is performance with the drop-shadow filter on larger images, though measurements suggest blur effects are relatively affordable. I'm setting up the camera system with different zoom behaviors—fixed position, zooming in, or zooming out—using a smooth interpolation curve that weights the travel distance differently depending on the camera mode.

For layer rendering, I'm sorting all layers by their depth value to establish the correct paint order, then building DOM elements for each layer positioned relative to either the front or back camera reference point. I need to use the original declaration index rather than the sorted index so images enter on their corresponding beats. When beats exist, I'll anchor to `beatTimes`, otherwise I'll spread the entry times evenly across the duration. Now I'm setting up the layout function to calculate aspect ratios from the loaded images.

Calculating dimensions based on whether it's a full-width layer or not, then positioning each element relative to the center of the canvas with left and top offsets.

In the animation loop, I'm applying a 3D camera transform that oscillates the view slightly based on time, then determining which layer should be in focus by checking which one has already passed through the entrance point.

For smooth focus transitions, I'm interpolating between layer depths using a smooth easing function that activates around each layer's entry time, creating a gradual shift rather than a jump. The layers need to be sorted by entry time for this focus chain to work correctly.

The depth of field effect scales based on how far each layer is from the current focus point, clamped to a reasonable range. Now I'm setting up the per-layer transform... Finishing the blur filter and confirming the 3D transform setup is correct — the leaf wrapper positioned in 3D space will blur its contents including the drop shadow, which is the intended effect. Now I need to restructure the tail section...

Setting up the boot function that calls `layoutLayers` and initializes the ready state, with a check for whether layers exist. I'm making sure `layoutLayers` is always defined even if there are no layers, and confirming that the badge centering with `offsetWidth` will work since layout happens synchronously. The stage's `overflow:hidden` clips the containers properly, and I need to account for how the existing parallax transform on `#bg` interacts with the absolute positioning of the new `.set` containers...

</details>

> 175	    .select("id, user_id, composition")
> 176	    .maybeSingle();

O que o cliente diz que \u00e9 N\u00c3O importa. */\nfunction sniffImageExt(bytes: Uint8Array): string | null {\n  if (bytes.length < 12) return null;\n  const b = bytes;\n  if (b[0] === 0x89 && b[1] === 0x50 && b[2] === 0x4e && b[3] === 0x47) return \"png\";\n  if (b[0] === 0xff && b[1] === 0xd8 && b[2] === 0xff) return \"jpg\";\n  if (b[0] === 0x52 && b[1] === 0x49 && b[2] === 0x46 && b[3] === 0x46\n      && b[8] === 0x57 && b[9] === 0x45 && b[10] === 0x42 && b[11] === 0x50) return \"webp\";\n  if (b[0] === 0x47 && b[1] === 0x49 && b[2] === 0x46 && b[3] === 0x38) return \"gif\";\n  return null;\n}\n\n/**\n * Baixa as camadas raster para o workDir e devolve os caminhos RELATIVOS que o HTML vai usar.\n *\n * FAIL-CLOSED por decreto (Amendment 43 \u00a7limites): o template referencia `layers/lN.ext` por\n * `file://`, e uma <img> que n\u00e3o existe N\u00c3O derruba a p\u00e1gina \u2014 sairiam 3.600 frames com buraco e o\n * job terminaria `done`. Aqui, qualquer camada que n\u00e3o baixe ou n\u00e3o seja imagem de verdade MATA o\n * render com o n\u00famero da camada no texto. O port\u00e3o do `__ready` no template \u00e9 a segunda linha; esta\n * \u00e9 a primeira, e \u00e9 a que d\u00e1 a mensagem \u00fatil (a edge fn j\u00e1 garantiu que o asset \u00e9 do dono).\n */\nasync function downloadLayers(\n  comp: MotionComposition,\n  workDir: string,\n): Promise<Array<{ src: string; plane: string; align: string; treatment: string; scale: number }>> {\n  const asked = Array.isArray(comp.layers) ? comp.layers : [];\n  if (!asked.length) return [];\n  mkdirSync(join(workDir, \"layers\"), { recursive: true });\n  const out: Array<{ src: string; plane: string; align: string; treatment: string; scale: number }> = [];\n  for (let i = 0; i < asked.length; i++) {\n    const L = asked[i];\n    const bucket = String(L?.bucket ?? \"\");\n    const key = String(L?.key ?? \"\");\n    if (!bucket || !key) throw new Error(`camada ${i + 1} sem origem (bucket/key ausentes)`);\n    const { data, error } = await supabase.storage.from(bucket).download(key);\n    if (error || !data) {\n      throw new Error(`camada ${i + 1} n\u00e3o baixou de ${bucket}/${key}: ${error?.message ?? \"sem corpo\"}`);\n    }\n    const bytes = new Uint8Array(await data.arrayBuffer());\n    const ext = sniffImageExt(bytes);\n    if (!ext) throw new Error(`camada ${i + 1} (${key}) n\u00e3o \u00e9 uma imagem reconhecida (png/jpg/webp/gif)`);\n    const rel = `layers/l${i}.${ext}`;\n    writeFileSync(join(workDir, rel), bytes);\n    out.push({\n      src: rel,\n      plane: L?.plane === \"fundo\" || L?.plane === \"frente\" ? L.plane : \"meio\",\n      align: L?.align === \"esq\" || L?.align === \"dir\" ? L.align : \"centro\",\n      treatment: L?.treatment === \"recorte\" ? \"recorte\" : \"laje\",\n      scale: Math.max(0.4, Math.min(1.8, Number(L?.scale) || 1)),\n    });\n  }\n  console.log(`\ud83e\uddf1 camadas montadas: ${out.length} (${out.map((l) => l.src).join(\", \")})`);\n  return out;\n}"
}

Actually, there's a cleaner geometric approach: express the alignment offset in each plane's own coordinate space so the on-screen result stays consistent across all depth layers. Since perspective scaling varies by depth—the front layer gets magnified by ~1.13× while the back layer shrinks to ~0.371×—the same CSS offset produces wildly different screen positions. I can normalize this by dividing the offset by the projection scale at that depth, which means far layers will need huge CSS offsets but that's fine since they're already distant.   "content": "# SOP \u2014 Cena Motion com camadas raster (\"MONTAR, n\u00e3o desenhar\")\n\n> **Lei 2 (Processo Antecipado).** Fonte da Verdade: `docs/bok/spaces-evolution/43-amendment-motion-montar-camadas.md`\n> (FR-SPACES-164..175). Se o operador n\u00e3o consegue fazer isto \u00e0 m\u00e3o sem errar, o motor tamb\u00e9m n\u00e3o.\n\n**ORO** \u2014 Operator: diretor de arte / creative-director (ou o Sovereign) \u00b7 Reviewer: Sovereign \u00b7\nOwner: engineer-spaces (o rail) + creative-director (a pe\u00e7a).\n\n---\n\n## 0. O que este processo entrega\n\nUm MP4 1920\u00d71080 (ou 1080\u00d71920) em que **pe\u00e7as prontas** \u2014 screenshot, arte gerada, recorte com\nalpha \u2014 s\u00e3o **montadas** num espa\u00e7o 3D com c\u00e2mera, parallax por geometria e profundidade de campo.\nCusto: **0 mco de render, US$ 0** (Chromium + FFmpeg no host). Sequence \u2014 a ordem, com crit\u00e9rio material de sucesso em cada passo\n\n1. **Ter a pe\u00e7a no acervo.** A camada aponta para um asset de `creative_assets` com `kind='image'`,\n   do pr\u00f3prio dono. Se a pe\u00e7a n\u00e3o existe: gerar (n\u00f3 de imagem), subir (Biblioteca) ou recortar\n   (passo 2). *Sucesso:* o asset aparece no seletor \"Adicionar imagem\".\n2. **(Opcional) Recortar com alpha.** `python3 scripts/motion/layered/matte.py <modelo.onnx> <in> <out.png> [--stroke 4]`\n   com os modelos em `/home/ubuntu/.mcorch/motion-models/`. *Sucesso:* o log imprime\n   `semi=<n>` > 0 e o PNG abre em modo `RGBA`. **Limite honesto:** o grafo do u2net infere em\n   320\u00d7320 fixo \u21d2 franja de 5\u20138 px em qualquer resolu\u00e7\u00e3o. O `--stroke` (contorno branco de papel)\n   **encobre** essa franja \u2014 \u00e9 o que o pr\u00f3prio `matte.py:56-58` documenta (\"hides matting fuzz by\n   design\"), e \u00e9 a est\u00e9tica da refer\u00eancia do Sovereign. N\u00e3o \u00e9 enfeite, \u00e9 curativo assumido.\n3. **Declarar cada camada** no inspector, em vocabul\u00e1rio FECHADO:\n   `plano` \u2208 {fundo, meio, frente} \u00b7 `lado` \u2208 {esq, centro, dir} \u00b7 `tratamento` \u2208 {laje, recorte} \u00b7\n   `tamanho` \u2208 [0,40 \u2026 1,80]. Uma curva mon\u00f3tona\n   consumida por TODOS os planos: o parallax \u00e9 consequ\u00eancia da geometria, nunca N transla\u00e7\u00f5es.\n5. **Ver antes de enfileirar.** `preview-motion-scene.ts` baixa as MESMAS pe\u00e7as e usa o MESMO motor.\n   *Sucesso:* o PNG do preview mostra as camadas montadas. **Este passo \u00e9 o que pega o que teste\n   nenhum pega** (enquadramento, colis\u00e3o, foco).\n6. **Renderizar.** Bot\u00e3o \"Renderizar anima\u00e7\u00e3o\" \u2192 `motion-render` \u2192 202 `queued` \u2192 worker.\n   *Sucesso:* `video_renders.state='done'` com `qa.layers = <n\u00ba de camadas>` e `storage_key` sob\n   `<uid>/motion/`.\n7. **Olhar o arquivo.** Extrair 2-3 frames (`ffmpeg -ss <t> -frames:v 1`) e **ver com os olhos**.\n   Nenhuma cena \u00e9 declarada pronta sem Vision QA ocular.\n\n## 3. Verification gates\n\n| Gate | Como se prova | Falha significa |\n|---|---|---|\n| **G1 \u2014 a pe\u00e7a \u00e9 do dono** | 422 `layer_not_found` para asset de outro tenant | vazamento cross-tenant |\n| **G2 \u2014 a pe\u00e7a \u00e9 imagem** | 422 `layer_not_found` para asset `kind='video'` | o worker baixaria um MP4 como `<img>` |\n| **G3 \u2014 camada sem id** | 422 `layer_invalid` | camada fantasma renderizando vazio |\n| **G4 \u2014 teto de 4** | 422 `too_many_layers` | or\u00e7amento de rel\u00f3gio do worker estourado |\n| **G5 \u2014 o download falhou** | o render termina `failed` com \"camada N n\u00e3o baixou\" | frames furados com job `done` |\n| **G6 \u2014 a imagem n\u00e3o decodificou** | `window.__fatal` no template \u2192 `render-frames.mjs` aborta | idem, pelo lado do browser |\n| **G7 \u2014 a perspectiva \u00e9 real** | raz\u00e3o borda-esq/borda-dir \u2260 1,0000 no DOM | `transform-style` achatado (ret\u00e2ngulo) |\n| **G8 \u2014 determinismo** | `buildSceneHtml(spec)` byte-id\u00eantico entre chamadas | `Math.random` infiltrado |\n\nAutomatizados em `src/test/motion-raster-layers.test.ts` (G7/G8 + a invariante de c\u00e2mera) e no\nwitness E2E (G1-G6). **G7 tem uma armadilha espec\u00edfica:** `getComputedStyle().transformStyle`\nreporta o valor *especificado* e continua dizendo `preserve-3d` mesmo quando o valor *usado* \u00e9\n`flat`. A \u00fanica prova \u00e9 **medir a caixa projetada** \u2014 marcadores 0\u00d70 nos cantos e comparar as\nalturas das bordas.\n\n## 4. Recovery path \u2014 falha no passo N\n\n| Sintoma | Causa prov\u00e1vel | A\u00e7\u00e3o exata |\n|---|---|---|\n| 422 `layer_not_found` | asset apagado / de outro tenant / `kind\u2260image` | reescolher a pe\u00e7a no seletor |\n| `failed`: \"camada N n\u00e3o baixou\" | objeto sumiu do Storage entre o enfileiramento e o claim | re-selecionar a pe\u00e7a e renderizar de novo |\n| `failed`: \"n\u00e3o \u00e9 uma imagem reconhecida\" | arquivo corrompido ou formato ex\u00f3tico (SVG/AVIF) | converter para PNG/JPEG e re-registrar |\n| `failed`: \"cena inv\u00e1lida: camada nao carregou\" | o arquivo baixou mas n\u00e3o decodifica | mesmo caminho acima |\n| render passa do or\u00e7amento | camadas grandes demais / cena longa | reduzir `tamanho`, cortar camadas, encurtar a cena |\n| pe\u00e7a fora do quadro | `lado` extremo num plano `frente` (que magnifica ~1,2\u00d7) | mudar para `centro` ou reduzir `tamanho` |\n\nTimeout do passo de frames: `FRAME_BUDGET_MS` em `scripts/motion-bridge.ts` (2,5\u00d7 o ms/frame\nMEDIDO). Depois do teto, o job morre e o reaper devolve \u00e0 fila \u2014 **n\u00e3o** reprocessa em sil\u00eancio.\n\n## 5. Success signal (materialmente observ\u00e1vel)\n\n`video_renders.state='done'` **E** `qa.layers = <n\u00ba declarado>` **E** um asset novo em\n`creative_assets` com `metadata.motion.layers = <n\u00ba>` **E** o frame extra\u00eddo mostrando as pe\u00e7as\nmontadas em profundidade. Os quatro juntos; tr\u00eas n\u00e3o bastam (o quarto \u00e9 o \u00fanico que prova o pixel).\n\n## 6. Custos medidos (nesta m\u00e1quina, 2026-08-06)\n\n| Item | Medida |\n|---|---|\n| Cena SEM camadas | 453 ms/frame (1920\u00d71080, jpeg q100) |\n| Cena com **3 camadas** | 497 ms/frame (**+10%**) |\n| Render de 9 s / 270 frames | 2 min 59 s de rel\u00f3gio, MP4 4,4 MB |\n| Custo em mco | **0** (o rail `motion` \u00e9 `charged_mco:0`) |\n| Custo das pe\u00e7as | `generateImage` = 20 mco cada \u00b7 upload/screenshot/matte = 0 |\n\nA lei de custo do motor \u00e9 **\u00c1REA de superf\u00edcie composta**, n\u00e3o \"efeito\": 3 camadas custam +44 ms/f\nporque somam superf\u00edcie, e n\u00e3o porque t\u00eam blur (todos os blurs somados d\u00e3o \u00b130 ms).\n\n## 7. Limites que este processo N\u00c3O resolve (declarados, n\u00e3o escondidos)\n\n- **Franja do matte** \u2014 320\u00d7320 fixo no grafo do u2net. O motor MONTAR virou nó do Spaces, ponta a ponta, com os 6 seams fechados. Nada foi commitado (há trabalho paralelo de outros agentes na mesma árvore).

## O que ficou vivo

**1 · Seam raster no motor** — `/home/gcrUX/htdocs/constellation-orchestra/scripts/motion/scene-template.ts`
Vocabulário FECHADO e versionado: `plane` {fundo −3400 · meio −2000 · frente −1050} · `align` {esq/centro/dir} · `treatment` {laje/recorte} · `scale` 0,4–1,8 · `camera` {aproxima/afasta/fixa}. Dois palcos com a MESMA câmera (`fundo`/`meio` atrás dos cards, `frente` na frente deles e atrás do HUD); ordem de pintura derivada do Z; DoF com estações na ordem de entrada; a camada entra no **beat** da mesma posição. A regra que o spike violava está travada em teste: no `.pl` só `will-change:transform` — opacidade e desfoque vivem na folha. Cena sem camadas **não emite palco nenhum** (zero regressão).

**2 · Transporte owner-scoped** — edge fn resolve `asset_id` → `creative_assets` `eq(user_id)` + `kind='image'` + key sob o prefixo do dono; o worker (`scripts/motion-bridge.ts` → `downloadLayers`) baixa, **sniffa a assinatura do arquivo** e escreve `layers/lN.ext` no workDir. Falha = render `failed` com o número da camada. Segunda linha: o template só sobe `__ready` depois que TODAS decodificaram e sobe `__fatal` se alguma falhar — e `render-frames.mjs` agora **espera pelos dois** (antes um `__fatal` viraria timeout mudo).

**3 · Inspector** — `MotionSceneInspector.tsx`: seletor real com miniaturas assinadas (bucket privado, `signStorageRef`), 3 selects de vocabulário + slider por camada, seletor de câmera. Card do nó declara `3 img`.

**4 · Custo** — segue **0 mco**; o rótulo não mudou de natureza, só ficou honesto: *"não consome mcoCoins (as imagens já foram pagas quando foram geradas)"*. Nenhum `node_run_id` é necessário — este rail é fila, não ledger.
